title: Mashed Potatoes
summary: Smooth, buttery mash, dried off in the hot pan before the butter and warm milk go in. The one that goes under the lamb shanks.

items.note: peeled and cut into 4 cm chunks

steps.text: Put the potatoes in a saucepan and cover them with cold water by 2-3 cm. Add the salt to the water.
Bring to the boil, then lower to a steady simmer and cook for {timer:15-20}, until a knife slides straight through the potatoes with no resistance.
Drain them very well, then put them back in the hot, empty saucepan over a low heat for {timer:1}, moving them around gently. This dries off the water and makes a much better mash.
Turn off the heat and mash thoroughly.
Mix in the butter, then the warm milk a little at a time. Stop adding milk when you like the consistency.
Season with the black pepper and the nutmeg, if using, then taste and add salt if it needs it.

tips: Never use a blender or a food processor: it makes the potatoes gluey.
The milk is a guide: anything from 120 to 150 ml, depending on the potatoes and how soft you like it. Start with a quarter teaspoon of pepper and add more to taste.
A small pinch of nutmeg works particularly well when the mash goes with lamb.
